decisionGate.question: Which minimum shared key grammar should Issue #31 ratify before implementation?
options: Ratify the strict bounded grammar: keys are nonblank and comma-free; comparison is exact and case-sensitive with no normalization; names/tokens are unique within each Judge array, Fixer array, and Reviewer scope list (duplicates rejected at the owning schema/argv seam); ordering is immaterial; alignment is exact set equality with no missing or extra key.

Ratify an alternate grammar, explicitly specifying all three currently open public behaviors: how comma-bearing keys are encoded and parsed, whether duplicates are rejected or canonicalized, and whether comparison is exact or normalized. Preserve the settled comma-separated CLI, opaque task/capability boundaries, and order-insensitive exact membership requirement.

details.note:
O1 is dismissed. Issue #31 already assigns current key-set reconciliation to the caller and leaves Fixer submission auditing/closure automation to #12. The package can enforce shape/minItems and the intrinsic state rule (`planned`/`refused` forbid `classesRepaired`; `completed` may carry it). The caller retains the typed Judge receipt and knows whether it made a class-bearing or direct no-class dispatch, so it can mechanically enforce contextual presence/absence and equality without parsing `--ak-fix-packet`. No typed Fixer key input is required.

O2 is sustained narrowly. The current authority does not determine observable handling of duplicate names/tokens, and an unescaped comma-separated argument cannot faithfully carry a comma-bearing Judge name. Case normalization is likewise not authorized or forbidden explicitly. These are public schema/argv and comparison semantics, so Judge cannot silently choose them. Ordering and alignment alone are already settled by “key set”: order is immaterial and equality permits neither missing nor extra keys. No topology, opaque-task, or capability decision is reopened.
